A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Causal2Vec and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Causal2Vec evaluations on MTEB, inference-efficiency measurements, and ablations, including additional analyses and per-dataset results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original MTEB evaluations, efficiency measurements, ablations, and appendix results. These retained outcomes qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The bidirectional encoder, MLP projection, Contextual token placement, Contextual/EOS representation concatenation, and contrastive objective remain unchanged in Section 3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same public retrieval training collection, 56 English MTEB datasets across seven tasks, and 41-dataset MTEB-MINI subset. No additional dataset or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 adds MGH as a scored Mistral-7B comparator in Table 1. All existing comparators remain, and the comparator sets in the other experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, benchmark composition, prompts, model configurations, sequence limits, and training budgets remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A–B. The MGH row supplies scores without documenting a separate new protocol.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendix C retain the same component, encoder-freezing, token-position, token-count, encoder-choice, representation-method, and token-norm analyses. Their evidence is unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing point estimates and averages across datasets retain the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds MGH's seven task scores and 65.87 MTEB average. Its classification score of 77.62 becomes the highest listed. Existing scores remain unchanged, including Causal2Vec-Mistral's 66.10 average and 66.85 with ICL, along with all appendix results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), their definitions, and the associated mathematical formulation are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about preserving causal attention, improving embeddings, achieving leading MTEB performance, and reducing sequence length and inference time.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning attention mismatch, recency bias, encoder freezing, and token redundancy remain unchanged, as do Appendix D's limitations. No interpretation of the newly added MGH results is supplied.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendices A–B retain the same model identifiers, hardware, optimizer and LoRA settings, training steps, sampling ratios, and instruction templates. No code or data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: v2 adds Pan et al.'s 'Negative matters: Multi-granularity hard-negative synthesis and anchor-token-aware pooling for enhanced text embeddings' as reference 47 for MGH. Other works are retained with subsequent references renumbered; the related-work discussion is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Manabu Okumura to the author list and updates the contact line and arXiv version/date stamp. The substantive prose, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains an MGH row and updates classification best/second-best highlighting. Minor table spacing and reference-page reflow accompany the revision; Figures 1–3 and the remaining table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Adding MGH modestly improves the comparison by exposing a strong competitor and its superior classification result, giving readers a fuller assessment of Causal2Vec. This benefit outweighs a limited consistency problem: Section 4.4 still names only bge-en-icl (few-shot) as an exception in its LLaMA-2 comparison, although MGH's 65.87 also exceeds that model's 64.94. The underlying method and original evidence remain unchanged.
